title: The SFS Identifiability Audit: What a Finite Site-Frequency Spectrum Can Identify About Population-Size History
shortTitle: What the site-frequency spectrum can and cannot say
oneLine: A finite site-frequency spectrum supplies only finitely many blurred averages of population history. This unrefereed candidate proves the corresponding identification boundary and reports a separate, setting-conditional audit of the disputed 900,000-year-old human bottleneck; it does not establish a model-free verdict on the event.
abstract: The site-frequency spectrum (SFS) compresses a genomic sample into allele-count frequencies and is widely used to reconstruct population-size history. This unrefereed candidate proves an exact boundary: over a broad positive class with scale fixed, a linear historical functional is point-identified by the exact finite-sample expected SFS if and only if its weight lies in the span of the sample's exponential kernels. An explicit rational-Laplace construction supplies distinct positive histories with identical expected spectra for every sample size, with a global Bernstein positivity certificate. The constructive replacement is certified reporting: resolution kernels and identified-set bounds from rank-reduced linear programmes carrying 50-digit dual certificates. A second implementation of the coalescence-to-SFS bridge, produced within the same workflow by a different mathematical route, provides implementation diversity but is not independent reproduction. A linked two-stage audit applies the machinery to nine published spectra from the disputed 930-813 kya human bottleneck. Stage one's protocol was frozen before real-data contact and rejects every spectrum under a millions-of-independent-sites error model. Stage two's linkage-aware error-model ladder was informed by stage-one diagnostics before its real-data interval endpoints were computed. At the most information-preserving declared setting, two YRI processings yield family-union depression-ratio intervals of [0.162, 0.934] and [0.132, 0.961], supporting depression and excluding the claimed severity conditional on that setting. CEU and CHB exclude the claimed severity there but do not establish depression. Across the full concession ladder the sets widen to uninformative.
narration: A site-frequency spectrum is a histogram of how often genetic variants appear in a sample. It contains only a finite number of blurred averages of population history. This unrefereed candidate proves an exact boundary: a historical quantity is pinned down by the expected finite spectrum only when its weight lies in the span of those blurs. The package also computes certified ranges for quantities outside that span. A second mathematical implementation checks the main data-model bridge, but both routes were produced in the same workflow. This is implementation diversity, not independent reproduction. A linked audit examines nine published spectra in the dispute over a severe human bottleneck about nine hundred thousand years ago. Stage one's protocol was frozen before real-data contact. Under an error model treating millions of sites as independent, no single-population history fits any spectrum. Stage two used an error-model ladder informed by stage-one diagnostics before any real-data interval endpoints were computed. At the most information-preserving declared setting, two Yoruba processings give depression-ratio intervals from point one six two to point nine three four, and point one three two to point nine six one. Those intervals support depression and exclude the claimed severity only under that setting. European and East Asian spectra exclude the claimed severity there but do not establish depression. Across the full ladder, the ranges become uninformative. The result is conditional on the declared model and deposited spectra. It is not a model-free verdict, has not been peer reviewed or rerun by an unaffiliated group, and this artificial-voice briefing is not additional evidence.

problem.name: Identifiability of population-size history from the site-frequency spectrum, and the disputed 930-813 kya human bottleneck

keyResults: Exact characterisation: a bounded linear historical functional is point-identified by the exact finite-n expected unfolded SFS if and only if its weight lies in the span of the n-1 exponential kernels, over a broad positive class with scale fixed.

An explicit rational-Laplace family gives distinct positive histories with identical expected spectra for every finite sample size; positivity is certified globally by a Bernstein polynomial bound (margin 0.1999 at epsilon 0.8).

Certified identified-set machinery: rank-reduced linear programmes whose every endpoint carries a 50-digit dual certificate and two-solver agreement; the v0.1.0 interval endpoints are superseded as artefacts of imposing noise-level equality directions.

A same-producer Tavare-formula implementation of the coalescence-to-SFS bridge agrees with the generator route at machine epsilon, with exact rational invertibility certificates and mutation controls; this is implementation diversity, not independent reproduction.

A severe bottleneck and a genuinely continuous piecewise-linear history within [0.504, 1.164] of baseline have normalised expected spectra at total-variation distance 4.70e-8: roughly 5e13 independent sites for an expected log-likelihood ratio of one.

Pre-registered audit stage one (frozen before data contact): universal class rejection - none of nine published spectra, including the bottleneck claimants' own, is reproducible by any single-population Kingman history under a multinomial error model; feasibility requires conceding an effective information content of roughly 5e2 to 3e4 independent sites.

Audit stage two used a disclosed linkage-aware error-model ladder informed by stage-one diagnostics before any real-data interval endpoints were computed. At the most information-preserving declared setting, two YRI processings yield family-union depression-ratio intervals of [0.162, 0.934] and [0.132, 0.961], supporting depression and excluding the claimed severity conditional on that setting; CEU and CHB exclude severity there but do not establish depression.

Across the full declared concession ladder the identified sets widen to uninformative. The empirical findings are setting-conditional and do not adjudicate the bottleneck independently of the error model and deposited spectra.
evidence: A 16-page candidate paper in PDF and TeX; Python operators and certified-bound machinery; a same-producer Tavare-formula implementation with exact rational certificates; rank-reduced linear programmes, Charnes-Cooper ratio programmes and Bernstein positivity certificates; 23 deterministic tests plus nine mutation and negative controls; explicit semantic receipt checks under ordinary and optimised Python; SHA-256 manifests; two protocol releases and two executed-audit releases over nine hash-verified published spectra; and public deviation ledgers. All checks and replays are producer-side.
statusDetail: Unrefereed candidate. Producer-side replay, mutation and negative controls, same-producer implementation diversity, exact rational certificates, two-solver agreement and high-precision dual certificates pass. Two unarchived model critiques informed earlier repairs but are not treated as external reviews. Stage one's protocol was frozen before real-data contact. Stage two's error-model form and parameter ladder were informed by stage-one real-data diagnostics before any stage-two real-data interval endpoints were computed. No unaffiliated group has reproduced any component; no independent reimplementation or population-genetics specialist review has been recorded; no proof has been formalised; bibliographic priority is not claimed. The audit findings are conditional on the declared error-model setting and deposited spectra, and the full concession ladder becomes uninformative.

availability.note: The corrected theorem package and four linked protocol or executed-audit records are publicly archived with versioned GitHub and Zenodo assets.

independentRerun.note: No unaffiliated party has rerun any archived package.

independentReimplementation.note: No implementation produced by an unaffiliated party has been assessed. The alternative Tavare-formula route is a same-producer implementation-diversity check.

formalVerification.note: No theorem or certificate checker has been formalised in a proof assistant.

specialistReview.note: No population-genetics or inverse-problems specialist has audited the theorem, the error models, or the audit conclusions.

editorialPeerReview.note: No journal or venue has conducted peer review.

dataEnvironmentReproducibility.note: Exact pinned dependencies replay on macOS arm64 and Ubuntu CI; float-laden receipts are byte-stable per platform but differ in final units across BLAS implementations, as documented in the audit repositories.

openProblems: Obtain an unaffiliated rerun and an independent reimplementation of the certified machinery and the audit chain.
Specialist review of the stage-two error model: a principled, pre-registered linkage and mispolarisation model replacing the disclosed data-informed ladders.
Extend the identification theorem and machinery to folded spectra, joint spectra across populations, and uncertain deep-time tails.
Formalise the finite-functional theorem, the null construction and the dual-certificate checker in a proof assistant.
A covariance-aware resolution-kernel audit on real data with genomic-block covariance, replacing the identity-covariance didactic examples.
A complete bibliographic priority review of the functional characterisation and the rational null family.

corrections.summary: Corrected the release's assurance and audit language. The alternative forward route is same-producer implementation diversity, not independent reproduction; the two model critiques are unarchived producer feedback, not external reviews; and the stage-two error-model ladder was informed by stage-one real-data diagnostics.
corrections.detail: The corrected page now distinguishes the theorem package from the linked empirical audit, limits the YRI interval interpretation to the most information-preserving declared setting, states that CEU and CHB exclude the claimed severity there without establishing depression, and notes that the full concession ladder is uninformative. decisionObject.description: An exact identifiability characterisation plus certified identified-set machinery and a two-stage pre-registered audit template for SFS-based demographic claims.
decisionObject.scope: Single-population unfolded-SFS inference under the neutral Kingman model; demonstrated on the nine published spectra of the 930-813 kya bottleneck dispute.

semanticBridge.description: The coalescence-to-SFS bridge is implemented twice from mathematically independent routes (generator matrix exponential; Tavare closed-form with exact rational coefficients) agreeing at machine epsilon, with eight mutation controls proving the comparison is live.
remainingRisks: Both bridge implementations were produced within the same workflow; an unaffiliated reimplementation is the outstanding rung.
The stage-two error model is disclosed as data-informed; a specialist-endorsed linkage and mispolarisation model could change the certified intervals.
The audit conclusions inherit the deposited spectra's own processing choices, which the audit treats as given.

humanJudgmentGates: Judge whether the declared error-model ladders are scientifically defensible concessions rather than tuned choices.
Assess novelty and priority of the functional characterisation and null construction beyond the bounded search.
Authorize each publication step, licensing and any applied or outreach use of the certified findings.
